summaryText:
Pastor Travis Hearn continued the Build My Church series with week three, a message titled "Skin in the Game." Starting from Jesus' promise in Matthew 16:18 that he will build his church, Pastor Travis reminded the congregation that Impact is not "my church" but "our church," and that there is a real difference between a visitor and an owner. Ownership changes how we care, give, and serve. He celebrated the grand opening of the South Scottsdale campus, thanked the church family for their sacrifice, prayer, and faith, and shared the 2027 theme word for Impact: deeper.

Using Haggai 1:4, he asked whether we pour our time, energy, and resources into good things like careers, families, and homes while neglecting the one thing that lasts for eternity, the church of Jesus Christ. He then gave four principles. First, God wants our firsts, not our leftovers, in time, talent, and treasure (Matthew 6:33 and Proverbs 3:9). Putting God first requires faith, because we trust him with everything that follows. Second, real sacrifice costs something. David refused to offer God a sacrifice that cost him nothing (2 Samuel 24), and his sacrifice became a place of worship for generations. Third, builders give by faith, not finances. The Macedonian churches in 2 Corinthians 8 gave joyfully, even beyond their ability, after first giving themselves to the Lord. Fourth, giving connects us to the vision. Citing Habakkuk 2:2, he restated Impact's vision to love God, love people, and make disciples, and said that vision without participation is just a dream somebody else is trying to build.

Closing with 2 Corinthians 9:6 and the principle of sowing and reaping, Pastor Travis offered a fresh angle. The greatest harvest of generosity may not be what God puts back into our hands, but what he does through our hands: salvations, healings, restored marriages, prodigals coming home, and generations coming to know Jesus. He prayed for a burden for the lost in our cities, neighborhoods, and workplaces. He invited anyone who wanted to give their life to Jesus to respond, and he prayed that God would shape the church into faithful kingdom builders. The message invites every listener, in the room and online, to move from watching to building and to ask, God, what are you asking of me?
mainPoints: This is our church, so every believer is called to be an owner with skin in the game, giving God our firsts (time, talent, and treasure) rather than our leftovers.
Real sacrifice costs something, and kingdom builders give by faith rather than by what they have, following the examples of David and the Macedonian churches.
Our giving connects us to the vision of loving God, loving people, and making disciples, and the greatest harvest of generosity is the lives God changes through us.

versesMentioned.text: And I tell you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not overcome it.
Is it a time for you yourselves to be living in your paneled houses, while this house remains a ruin?
You shall have no other gods before me.
But seek first his kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well.
Honor the Lord with your wealth, with the firstfruits of all your crops;
In everything I did, I showed you that by this kind of hard work we must help the weak, remembering the words the Lord Jesus himself said: 'It is more blessed to give than to receive.'
For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life.
"Come," he said. Then Peter got down out of the boat, walked on the water and came toward Jesus.

But the king replied to Araunah, "No, I insist on paying you for it. I will not sacrifice to the Lord my God burnt offerings that cost me nothing." So David bought the threshing floor and paid fifty shekels of silver for it.

And now, brothers and sisters, we want you to know about the grace that God has given the Macedonian churches. In the midst of a very severe trial, their overflowing joy and their extreme poverty welled up in rich generosity. For I testify that they gave as much as they were able, and even beyond their ability. Entirely on their own, they urgently pleaded with us for the privilege of sharing in this service to the Lord's people. And they exceeded our expectations: They gave themselves first of all to the Lord, and then by the will of God also to us. So we urged Titus, just as he had earlier made a beginning, to bring also to completion this act of grace on your part. But since you excel in everything, in faith, in speech, in knowledge, in complete earnestness and in the love we have kindled in you, see that you also excel in this grace of giving.
Then the Lord replied: "Write down the revelation and make it plain on tablets so that a herald may run with it."
Remember this: Whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows generously will also reap generously.
His master replied, "Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things. Come and share your master's happiness!"

Monday.scripture: Matthew 6:33: "But seek first his kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well."
Monday.focus: Putting God first in my time.
Monday.action: Before checking your phone or social media this morning, spend at least five minutes reading a passage of Scripture and praying. Repeat this each morning this week.
Monday.prayer: Lord, you are first in my life. Help me start each day with you and trust you to add what I need.

Tuesday.scripture: Proverbs 3:9: "Honor the Lord with your wealth, with the firstfruits of all your crops."
Tuesday.focus: Giving God my first, not my leftovers.
Tuesday.action: Look over your budget and prayerfully decide on a first portion to set aside for God's work before other spending. If you are already giving, thank God for the opportunity.
Tuesday.prayer: Father, everything I have comes from you. Teach me to honor you with my first and to trust you with the rest.

Wednesday.scripture: 2 Samuel 24:24: "I will not sacrifice to the Lord my God burnt offerings that cost me nothing."
Wednesday.action: Choose one way to give of your time or resources that takes real effort, such as serving at church, helping a neighbor, or giving up something you enjoy to bless someone else.
Wednesday.prayer: Lord, keep me from offering you only what is convenient. Give me a willing heart to sacrifice for your kingdom.

Thursday.scripture: 2 Corinthians 8:3: "For I testify that they gave as much as they were able, and even beyond their ability."
Thursday.focus: Giving by faith, not by what I have.
Thursday.action: Ask God to show you one act of generosity to take by faith today, such as meeting a need, sending an encouraging note, or giving toward a ministry. Then take that step.
Thursday.prayer: God, give me the joy and faith of the Macedonian believers. Help me give myself to you first, and then to others.

Friday.scripture: Habakkuk 2:2: "Write down the revelation and make it plain on tablets so that a herald may run with it."
Friday.focus: Connecting to the vision: love God, love people, make disciples.
Friday.action: Write down Impact's vision (love God, love people, make disciples) and place it where you will see it. Then invite one person to a service or the online campus.
Friday.prayer: Lord, help me run with the vision you have given our church. Show me where I can participate, not just watch.

Saturday.scripture: 2 Corinthians 9:6: "Whoever sows generously will also reap generously."
Saturday.focus: Praying for a harvest of changed lives.
Saturday.action: Write down the names of three people who need Jesus and pray for them. Ask God how you can encourage or serve them this coming week, and plan to bring someone with you on Sunday.
Saturday.prayer: Father, give me a burden for the lost and a heart that sows generously. Use my hands to change lives for your glory.

title: Why God Wants Your First, Not Your Leftovers | Skin in the Game
